security_audit.summary: All eight static alerts are false positives caused by Markdown code fences or inline code, with no shell or Ruby execution present. The workflow has one medium-risk business concern because it can consume about 660 BotSee credits without an explicit confirmation step.

remediation.issue: The analysis step can consume about 660 BotSee credits without explicit confirmation immediately before execution.
remediation.suggestion: Show the expected credit cost and request user approval before running the BotSee analysis.

Lines 24 through 26 are a fenced Markdown example containing a BotSee slash command. Backticks only format documentation and do not invoke a shell.
The backticks at line 26 close a Markdown code fence. No Ruby expression or executable shell construct is present.
Line 34 formats a BotSee slash command as inline Markdown code. The text documents a plugin operation and does not perform shell execution.
Line 38 uses inline backticks around a flag and BotSee slash command. These are documentation literals without an execution mechanism.
Lines 46 through 48 form a Markdown code block for the BotSee analysis command. The fence itself cannot execute external commands.
The backticks at line 48 close a documentation code block. They are not Ruby command substitution or shell syntax.
Lines 54 through 57 present two BotSee result commands inside a Markdown fence. No code in the skill directly launches either command.

content.user_title: Audit Your Website for AI Search Visibility
content.value_statement: AI search engines may overlook a brand when its website language differs from common queries and cited sources. This skill uses BotSee evidence to identify gaps and propose focused copy changes.
actual_capabilities: Creates a BotSee site with customer types, personas, and generated questions.
Reviews and replaces generic questions with queries that reflect audience search intent.
Runs BotSee analysis to collect competitor, keyword, and source data.
Finds keyword and citation opportunities where a brand is missing or ranks poorly.
Compares a live homepage with AI search terminology and competitor language.
Proposes focused copy edits for titles, headlines, features, sections, and integrations.
limitations: Requires the separate BotSee plugin and sufficient BotSee credits.
BotSee analysis consumes about 660 credits per documented run.
Results depend on generated questions and the available BotSee analysis data.
The workflow focuses on homepage copy and does not change page structure.

use_cases.title: Assess Brand Visibility
use_cases.description: Measure where a brand appears across AI search questions and identify missing terminology.

use_cases.title: Improve Landing Page Copy
use_cases.description: Compare homepage language with AI queries and add relevant terms through focused text changes.

use_cases.title: Find Citation Opportunities
use_cases.description: Discover sources that AI engines cite when they omit the audited brand.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Visibility Audit
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the AI search visibility of [domain]. Show the expected BotSee credit cost before starting any paid analysis.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner wants a clear overview of brand visibility.

prompt_templates.title: Review Search Questions
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the BotSee questions for [domain] and [audience]. Draft more realistic questions for my approval before creating them.
prompt_templates.scenario: A marketer wants stronger questions before analysis.

prompt_templates.title: Find Homepage Language Gaps
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare [domain] with the latest BotSee keyword opportunities. Present missing terms, supporting evidence, and minimal homepage copy changes.
prompt_templates.scenario: A content strategist needs evidence-based copy recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Complete Optimization Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit [domain] for [audiences]. Analyze keyword and source opportunities, compare competitors, and prepare prioritized copy changes without editing until I approve.
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced user needs a complete AI visibility workflow.

output_examples.input: Audit example.com for AI visibility and identify homepage terminology gaps.
output_examples.output: The audit highlights missing category terms, shows supporting search questions, and proposes focused updates to the title, hero text, and features.

output_examples.input: Find source opportunities for our enterprise monitoring product.
output: Industry publication: cited by AI answers that omit the brand.
Technical directory: relevant to enterprise monitoring comparisons.
Partner site: potential integration and citation opportunity.

output_examples.input: Improve our BotSee questions for developer audiences.
output_examples.output: The revised question set emphasizes APIs, integrations, deployment workflows, pricing, and technical comparisons. The skill requests approval before creating questions.

best_practices: Confirm the target domain, audiences, and expected BotSee credit cost before analysis.
Review draft questions with the user before creating or replacing them.
Link every proposed copy change to specific keyword, query, competitor, or source evidence.
anti_patterns: Do not run paid analysis without showing the expected credit cost and receiving approval.
Do not add unsupported keywords only to increase term frequency.
Do not change page layout, structure, or unrelated code during focused copy optimization.

faq.question: What does this skill audit?
faq.answer: It audits brand visibility, keyword gaps, competitor presence, cited sources, and homepage language across BotSee AI search data.

faq.question: Which AI tools support this skill?
faq.answer: The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Does this skill require another plugin?
faq.answer: Yes. The BotSee plugin must be installed and its slash commands must be available.

faq.question: Does the analysis use paid credits?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented BotSee analysis costs about 660 credits, so confirm the cost before execution.

faq.question: Will the skill redesign my website?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on text changes and explicitly avoids layout or structural changes.

faq.question: Can it publish changes automatically?
faq.answer: The workflow compiles, commits, and pushes only after user approval. Repository access and appropriate permissions are still required.
